draft.title: Contingency planning
card: A contingency plan is a set of steps a business prepares in case something goes wrong. The problem may never happen, but the business is ready if it does.
Managers start by listing events that could harm the business, such as a main supplier failing, a power outage or a fire. They then judge how likely each is and how badly it would hurt.
For each serious risk, the plan sets out what to do, who does it and what resources are needed. An example is a backup supplier that has already been approved.
Because the response is planned in advance, the business can act quickly and limit the damage. The plan should be reviewed from time to time so it stays up to date.
draft.remember: A contingency plan is a prepared response to a problem that might happen.

a.q: Which action is an example of contingency planning?
opts: Arranging a backup supplier in case the main one fails
Comparing this month's sales with the sales target
Copying the prices of the largest competitor
Ordering extra stock after a supplier has closed
a.why: Preparing a backup supplier before any problem happens is a planned response to a possible event. Ordering stock after the supplier has closed is a reaction, not a plan made in advance.
a.clue: Look for the action taken before anything goes wrong.

b.q: Mia runs a bakery in Dubbo with one oven. She writes down what she will do if the oven breaks: who to call, and a nearby bakery that has agreed to bake her bread. Why is this useful?
opts: She can keep trading quickly if the oven fails
It stops the oven from ever breaking down
It shows how her sales compare with other bakeries
It means she no longer needs to insure the oven
b.why: The plan sets out the response before the breakdown, so Mia can act fast and limit lost sales. A plan cannot prevent a fault, and it does not compare her with others.
b.clue: Think about what the plan changes if the oven does break.

a.best: Arranging a backup supplier in case the main one fails

b.best: She can keep trading quickly if the oven fails
